You're tracking the right mechanism. **Persistent friction across the pes anserinus bursa** from valgus knee stress and tight hamstrings **creates microtrauma that outpaces repair**. Now overlay **poorly controlled diabetes**: hyperglycemia impairs neutrophil chemotaxis and phagocytosis, turning the bursal fluid into a **pro-inflammatory, non-healing soup**. That's not sublimal — that's the **reason NSAIDs alone often fail here**: they blunt prostaglandin-mediated pain but don't fix the **metabolic milieu**. Steroids work by **dampening local cytokine cascades**, but only after you've **confirmed no septic bursitis** (rule-out: erythema spreading, fever, leukocytosis). So yes: **ice for acute vasoconstriction**, **relative rest to offload the bursa**, **short-course oral NSAID**, and **local steroid injection only if afebrile and no cellulitis**. The diabetes means healing will be delayed — you're buying time for the bursa to resorb the irritant.
